country.name: Netherlands
country.tagline: Limburg marl, Achterhoek farms and fungus-resistant grapes: Dutch wine is young, small and growing fast.

stats.note: CBS via FAOSTAT (official figure): 230 ha of vines in 2024 (250 ha in 2023). Wikipedia (de) put output at about 1.2 million bottles in 2020; no current production figure found

country.overview:
Wine in the Netherlands is first documented in 968, and medieval vineyards grew on the slopes around Maastricht and along the Maas and Geul, but beer, the Little Ice Age and phylloxera finished them; the last old vineyard near Maastricht closed in 1946. The revival began in the 1970s, when the Apostelhoeve near Maastricht planted Müller-Thurgau and Riesling on the marl slopes of the Louwberg, and has accelerated with warmer summers. By 2020 there were about 250 hectares in some 135 sites, producing around 1.2 million bottles, and the area has kept growing.

Two very different styles have emerged. In South Limburg, on chalky marl (mergel) hills like those across the border in Belgium, classic varieties such as Auxerrois, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir dominate. Elsewhere, on sandy soils in Gelderland, Overijssel and North Brabant, growers rely on fungus-resistant varieties (Solaris, Johanniter, Souvignier Gris, Regent, Cabernet Cortis) that can be farmed with little or no spraying. Each style now has PDOs: Mergelland, Vijlen and the cross-border Maasvallei Limburg in Limburg, and Oolde, Ambt Delden and Achterhoek-Winterswijk in the east, most of them single estates.

history.title: First record of Dutch wine
history.text: The first mention of viticulture in the Netherlands dates to 968; medieval vineyards grew around Maastricht and on Maas and Geul slopes.

history.title: The last old vineyard
history.text: The last historic vineyard near Maastricht closed, ending the old tradition.

history.title: Apostelhoeve replants
history.text: The Hulst family planted vines at the Apostelhoeve on the Louwberg south of Maastricht, the start of modern Dutch wine.

history.title: PDOs arrive
history.text: Maasvallei Limburg (2017, with Belgium), Mergelland (2018), Vijlen and Oolde (2018), Ambt Delden (2019) and Achterhoek-Winterswijk (2020) were registered.

country.classification: Six PDOs registered between 2017 and 2020: Maasvallei Limburg (cross-border with Belgium), Mergelland, Vijlen, Oolde, Ambt Delden and Achterhoek-Winterswijk. Each province has a PGI-level regional wine. Several PDOs are effectively single estates with strict rules on varieties and yields.
country.climate_soils: A cool maritime climate. South Limburg's hills of Cretaceous chalky marl (mergel) and loess give the most classic conditions; the east and centre have sand, loam and glacial deposits, where wet summers favour fungus-resistant varieties.

grapes.name: Solaris, Johanniter, Souvignier Gris
grapes.note: Fungus-resistant whites, the most planted grapes in sandy regions.

grapes.name: Auxerrois, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir

further_reading: Wijnbouw in Nederland (KNVW, Royal Dutch Wine Growers Association)

regions.name: Limburg (NL)
regions.tagline: Marl hills, the Maas and the classic varieties.
regions.summary: South Limburg is the most hilly part of the Netherlands and the historic heart of Dutch wine, with vineyards on chalky marl and loess near Maastricht, Valkenburg, Gulpen and Vaals. The Mergelland and Vijlen PDOs cover it, and the Maasvallei Limburg PDO covers the river valley further north around Thorn and Roermond.
regions.history: Medieval vineyards on the Maas slopes, revived from 1970 by the Apostelhoeve.
regions.terroir: Cretaceous marl and loess, Maas gravels.
regions.grapes: Auxerrois, Pinot Gris, Pinot Blanc, Riesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Solaris, Johanniter.

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

regions.name: Eastern Netherlands
regions.tagline: Farm estates on sand, built on fungus-resistant grapes.
regions.summary: The eastern provinces of Gelderland and Overijssel have some of the largest Dutch vineyards, on sandy and loamy soils, with three single-estate PDOs: Oolde near Lochem, Ambt Delden in Twente and Achterhoek-Winterswijk.
regions.history: A twenty-first-century development, driven by farmers diversifying from dairy and arable crops.
regions.terroir: Sand, loam and glacial deposits; cool, wet maritime climate.
regions.grapes: Solaris, Johanniter, Souvignier Gris, Cabernet Blanc, Regent, Pinotin, Cabernet Cortis.
regions.styles: Dry whites, sparkling, reds, some fortified and dried-grape wines.

sources.title: Candiago et al. (2022), geospatial inventory of EU wine PDOs (registration dates, varieties, communes)

nl-achterhoek-winterswijk.name: Achterhoek - Winterswijk
nl-achterhoek-winterswijk.grapes: Acolon, Cabernet Cortis, Cabertin, Johanniter, Merzling, Monarch, Pinotin, Regent, Solaris, Souvignier Gris
nl-achterhoek-winterswijk.summary: The PDO for Winterswijk in the eastern Achterhoek near the German border, registered in 2020, with fungus-resistant varieties grown on unusual soils that include Muschelkalk limestone, rare in the Netherlands. Wijngaard Hesselink is the main producer.
nl-achterhoek-winterswijk.terroir: Sand, loam and pockets of shell limestone at Winterswijk.
nl-achterhoek-winterswijk.nerd_note: Winterswijk has one of the very few Muschelkalk outcrops in the Netherlands, quarried for its stone and famous for its Triassic fossils.

nl-ambt-delden.name: Ambt Delden
nl-ambt-delden.grapes: Johanniter, Solaris, Souvignier Gris, Regent, Pinotin
nl-ambt-delden.summary: A single-estate PDO in Hof van Twente, Overijssel, registered in 2019 for Wijngaard Hof van Twente, using only fungus-resistant varieties, including wine from raisined grapes.
nl-ambt-delden.terroir: Sandy and loamy soils of Twente.

nl-maasvallei-limburg.name: Maasvallei Limburg
nl-maasvallei-limburg.grapes: Auxerrois, Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Noir, Dornfelder, Acolon
nl-maasvallei-limburg.summary: The EU's first cross-border PDO, shared with Belgian Limburg along the Maas. On the Dutch side it includes Maasgouw (Thorn), Echt-Susteren, Roermond, Leudal, Sittard-Geleen and Stein.
nl-maasvallei-limburg.nerd_note: Entry also listed under Belgium; the polygon spans both countries.

nl-mergelland.name: Mergelland
nl-mergelland.grapes: Auxerrois, Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris, Riesling, Müller-Thurgau, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Noir, Pinot Noir Précoce, Dornfelder
nl-mergelland.summary: Mergelland, registered in 2018, covers nine municipalities of South Limburg around Maastricht, Valkenburg and Gulpen, on the chalky marl (mergel) that is quarried for building stone here. It allows only classic vinifera varieties, capped at 85 hl/ha, and includes the Apostelhoeve, the oldest modern Dutch vineyard.
nl-mergelland.terroir: Cretaceous marl and loess on slopes of the Maas, Geul and Jeker valleys.
nl-mergelland.nerd_note: The marl caves (grotten) around Maastricht, such as those under Château Neercanne, have long served as natural wine cellars.

nl-oolde.name: Oolde
nl-oolde.grapes: Solaris, Cabernet Blanc, Regent, Pinotin, Cabertin
nl-oolde.summary: Oolde is the single-estate PDO of Wijngoed Hof te Oolde near Laren (Lochem) in Gelderland, registered in 2018. It allows only fungus-resistant varieties, a statement of organic intent, and includes still, sparkling, semi-sparkling and liqueur wines.
nl-oolde.terroir: Sand and loam on the moraine ridge near Lochem.
nl-oolde.nerd_note: One of the first PDOs anywhere based entirely on fungus-resistant (PIWI) varieties.

nl-vijlen.name: Vijlen
nl-vijlen.grapes: Solaris, Johanniter, Souvignier Gris, Cabernet Blanc, Muscaris, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Cortis, Monarch, Baron, Pinotin
nl-vijlen.summary: Vijlen is a single-estate PDO (2018) near Vaals, at about 200 metres on the slopes of the highest hills in the Netherlands, close to the German and Belgian borders. It is farmed by Wijngaard St. Martinus with a mix of classic and fungus-resistant grapes; yields are capped at 55 hl/ha.
nl-vijlen.terroir: Loess and gravel on south-facing slopes near the Vaalserberg.
nl-vijlen.nerd_note: Among the highest vineyards in the Netherlands.

sites.name: Apostelhoeve
sites.class: PDO Mergelland; oldest modern Dutch vineyard (1970)
sites.text: A farm estate on the Louwberg south of Maastricht where the Hulst family planted vines in 1970, beginning the modern Dutch wine revival.

sites.name: Wijngaard St. Martinus
sites.text: A vineyard on the slopes near Vijlen in the Limburg hills, the sole producer of the Vijlen PDO.

sites.name: Wijngoed Thorn
sites.text: A vineyard and tasting room in the white-washed village of Thorn on the Maas, one of the leading Dutch estates.

sites.name: Hof te Oolde
sites.text: A large estate near Laren in Gelderland, farmed with fungus-resistant grapes and holder of the Oolde PDO.

sites.name: Wijngaard Hof van Twente
sites.text: A Twente estate near Bentelo, sole producer of the Ambt Delden PDO.

sites.name: Wijngaard Hesselink
sites.text: A family vineyard at Winterswijk-Henxel, the main producer of the Achterhoek-Winterswijk PDO.

sites.name: Wageningse Berg vineyard
sites.text: A vineyard on the moraine slope of the Wageningse Berg above the Rhine, linked to the town's agricultural tradition.
